mn92:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was wandering in the country of the Anguttarāpans with a large Sangha of bhikkhus, with twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus. There is town of the Anguttarāpans called Apaṇa where the Blessed One eventually arrived.
mn92:2.2: ‘The monk Gotama, it seems, the son of the Sakyans who went forth from a Sakyan clan, has been wandering in the country of the Anguttarāpans with a large Sangha of bhikkhus, with twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus, and he has come to Apaṇa.
mn92:2.3: Now a good report of Master Gotama has been spread to this effect:
mn92:2.4: “That Blessed One is such since he is Arahant, Fully Enlightened, perfect in true knowledge and conduct, sublime, knower of worlds, incomparable leader of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and men, enlightened, blessed.”
mn92:2.5: He describes this world with its gods, its Māras, and its (Brahmā) Divinities, this generation with its monks and divines, with its kings and its men, which he has himself realized through direct knowledge.
mn92:2.6: He teaches a Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle and good in the end with (the right) meaning and phrasing, he affirms a life divine that is utterly perfect and pure.
mn92:2.7: Now it is good to see such Arahants.’
mn92:3.1: Then the matted-hair ascetic Keniya went to the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him,
mn92:3.2: and when the courteous and amiable talk was finished he sat down at one side.
mn92:3.3: When he had done so, the Blessed One instructed, urged, roused and encouraged him with talk on the Dhamma.
mn92:3.4: Then delighting in the Blessed One’s words and agreeing, the matted-hair ascetic Keniya said to the Blessed One:
mn92:3.5: ‘Let the Blessed One, together with the Sangha of bhikkhus, accept tomorrow’s meal from me.’
mn92:3.6: When this was said, the Blessed One told him:
mn92:3.7: ‘The Sangha of bhikkhus is large, Keniya, there are twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus and you place all your confidence in the divines.’
mn92:3.8: A second time the matted-hair ascetic said to the Blessed One:
mn92:3.9: ‘Although the Sangha of bhikkhus is large, Master Gotama, and there are twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus, and although I place all my confidence in the divines,
mn92:3.10: still let the Blessed One, together with the Sangha of bhikkhus, accept tomorrow’s meal from me.’
mn92:3.11: A second time the Blessed One told him:
mn92:3.12: ‘The Sangha of bhikkhus is large, Keniya, there are twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus. And you place all your confidence in the divines.’
mn92:3.13: A third time the matted-hair ascetic said to the Blessed One:
mn92:3.14: ‘Although the Sangha of bhikkhus is large, Master Gotama, and there are twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus, and although I place all my confidence in the divines,
mn92:3.15: still let the Blessed One, together with the Sangha of bhikkhus, accept tomorrow’s meal from me.’
mn92:3.16: The Blessed One accepted in silence.
mn92:4.1: Then, knowing that the Blessed One had accepted, he rose from his seat and went to his own hermitage where he addressed his friends and companions, relatives and kin:
mn92:4.2: ‘Hear me, my friends and companions, relatives and kin;
mn92:4.3: ‘The monk Gotama has been invited by me for tomorrow’s meal together with the Sangha of bhikkhus.
mn92:4.4: Make the necessary purchases and preparations for me.’
mn92:4.5: ‘Yes, sir,’ they replied, and some excavated ovens, some chopped wood, some washed dishes, some set out water pots, some prepared seats,
mn92:4.6: while the matted-hair ascetic Keniya himself got ready a pavilion tent.
mn92:5.1: Now on that occasion Sela of the divine caste was staying at Āpaṇa. An expert in the Three Vedas, he knew the text and context of the Histories, the fifth (of the divine authorities), with their invocations, liturgy, word-analysis, and he was fully versed in Natural Science and that of the Marks of the Great Man. He had three hundred divine-caste students to recite hymns.
mn92:6.1: On that occasion the matted-hair ascetic Keniya placed all his confidence in Sela the divine.
mn92:6.2: Then Sela of the divine caste, attended by three hundred divine-caste students, was walking and wandering for exercise, and he came to the matted-hair ascetic Keniya’s hermitage.
mn92:6.3: He saw there some excavating ovens, some chopping wood, some washing dishes, some setting out water pots, some preparing seats, while the matted-hair ascetic Keniya himself was getting ready a pavilion tent.
mn92:7.1: When he saw this, he asked the matted-hair ascetic Keniya:
mn92:7.2: ‘What, is there a taking in marriage or a giving in marriage? Or is there some great sacrifice? Or has Seniya Bimbisāra king of Magadha been invited with a large retinue for tomorrow’s meal?’
mn92:8.1: ‘I have no taking in marriage or giving in marriage, Sela; nor has Seniya Bimbisāra king of Magadha been invited with a large retinue for tomorrow’s meal.
mn92:8.2: But I have a great sacrifice.
mn92:8.3: The monk Gotama who went forth from the Sakyan clan has been wandering in the country of the Anguttarāpans with a large Sangha of bhikkhus, with twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus, and has come to Āpaṇa.
mn92:8.4: Now a good report of Master Gotama has spread to this effect:
mn92:8.5: “That Blessed One is such since he is Arahant, Fully Enlightened, perfect in true knowledge and conduct, sublime, knower of worlds, incomparable leader of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and men, enlightened, blessed.”
mn92:8.6: He has been invited by me for tomorrow’s meal, together with the Sangha of bhikhus.’
mn92:10.1: Then it occurred to Sela of the divine caste:
mn92:10.2: ‘This news “Enlightened One” is hard to get in the world.
mn92:10.3: Now the thirty-two Marks of the Great Man have been handed down in our hymns, and the Great Man who is endowed with them has only two possible destinies, no other.
mn92:10.4: If he lives the home life he becomes an ideal king of Dhamma, master of the four quarters, all-victorious, who has stabilized his country, and possesses seven treasures—
mn92:10.6: the Wheel Treasure, the Elephant Treasure, the Horse Treasure, the Jewel Treasure, the Woman Tresure, the Householder Treasure, and the Steward Treasure as the seventh—
mn92:10.7: his children who exceed a thousand, brave and heroic, crush the armies of others;
mn92:10.8: over the earth bounded by this ocean he rules without a rod, without a weapon and in the Dhamma.
mn92:10.9: But if he goes forth from the home life into homelessness, he becomes an Arahant, a Fully Enlightened One, who draws aside the veil in the world.’
mn92:11.1: He said: ‘My good Keniya, where is Master Gotama, Arahant and Fully Enlightened, living now?’
mn92:11.2: When this was said, the matted-hair ascetic Keniya extended his right arm and said:
mn92:11.3: ‘There, where that green line (of trees) is, Master Sela.’
mn92:12.1: Then Sela of the divine caste went with the three hundred divine-caste students to the Blessed One.
mn92:12.2: Then he addressed the divine-caste students:
mn92:12.4: for Blessed Ones are difficult of access, they walk alone like lions.
mn92:12.5: And when I am in converse with the monk Gotama, let there be no interrupting me with talk meanwhile,
mn92:12.6: but wait until our talk has been completed.’
mn92:13.1: Then Sela of the divine caste went to the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him,
mn92:13.2: and when the courteous and amiable talk was finished he sat down at one side.
mn92:13.3: When had done so, he looked for the thirty-two Marks of the Great Man on the Blessed One’s body.
mn92:13.4: He saw more or less, the thirty-two Marks of the Great Man on the Blessed One’s body, except for two;
mn92:13.5: he was doubtful and uncertain about two of the marks, and he could not decide and make up his mind about them:
mn92:13.6: about what should be hidden by a cloth being enclosed in a sheath, and about the largeness of the tongue.
mn92:13.7: It occurred to the Blessed One:
mn92:13.8: ‘This Sela of the divine caste sees, more or less, the thirty-two Marks of the Great Man on me, except for two;
mn92:13.9: he is doubtful and uncertain about two of the marks, and he cannot decide and make up his mind about them:
mn92:13.10: about what should be hidden by a cloth being enclosed in a sheath, and about the largeness of the tongue.’
mn92:14.1: Then the Blessed One worked such a feat of supernormal success that Sela of the divine caste saw that in the Blessed One what should be hidden by a cloth was enclosed in a sheath.
mn92:14.2: Then the Blessed One extended his tongue, and he repeatedly touched both earholes, both nostrils, and he covered the whole of his forehead with his tongue.
mn92:15.1: Sela of the divine caste thought:
mn92:15.2: ‘The monk Gotama is endowed with the thirty-two Marks of the Great Man, they are complete, not incomplete.
mn92:15.3: But I do not know whether he is enlightened or not.
mn92:15.4: However, I have heard from the elders, the aged divines, who preach according to the line of teachers,
mn92:15.5: that those who are Arahant and Fully Enlightened manifest themselves as such when their praise is spoken.
mn92:15.6: Suppose I eulogize the monk Gotama to his face with fitting stanzas?’
mn92:15.7: Then he eulogized the Blessed One to his face with fitting stanzas:

mn92:24.1: And Sela of the divine caste with his following, received the Going-forth under the Blessed One, and received the Full Admission.
mn92:25.1: Then when the night was ended, the matted-hair ascetic Keniya had good food of various kinds prepared in his own hermitage and he had the time announced to the Blessed One:
mn92:25.2: ‘It is time, Master Gotama, the meal is ready.’
mn92:25.3: Then, it being morning, the Blessed One dressed, and taking his bowl and (outer) robe, he went with the Sangha of bhikkhus to the hermitage of the matted-hair ascetic Keniya and he sat down on the seat made ready.
mn92:25.4: Then with his own hands the matted-hair ascetic Keniya served and satisfied the Sangha of bhikkhus headed by the Enlightened One with the good food of various kinds.
mn92:25.5: Then when the Blessed One had eaten and no longer had the bowl in his hand, the matted-hair ascetic Keniya took a low seat and sat down at one side.
mn92:25.6: When he had done so, the Blessed One gave him his blessing with these stanzas:
mn92:26.1: ‘Burnt offering is the glory of fires,
mn92:26.3: Glory of human beings, a king,
mn92:26.4: Glory of flowing rivers, the sea;
mn92:26.5: The moon is glory of the stars,
mn92:26.6: The sun is glory of all that shine;
mn92:26.7: Merit is glory of all who aspire;
mn92:26.8: The Sangha, glory of those who give.’
mn92:26.9: Then when the Blessed One had given his blessing with these stanzas, he rose from his seat and departed.
mn92:27.1: Now not long after his Full Admission, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and strenuous, the venerable Sela, with his following, by realization themselves with direct knowledge, here and now entered upon and abode in that supreme goal of the life divine for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness.
mn92:27.2: He knew directly: ‘Birth is exhausted, the life divine has been lived out, what was to be done is done, there is no more of this to come’.
mn92:27.3: And the venerable Sela became one of the Arahants, together with his following.
